description: Make the shell-write redirect scan heredoc-, quote-, and comment-aware (masking bodies/spans/comments) so prose quoting a redirect is no longer denied, while real writes stay detected
deviation_notes: All 11 top-level tasks are done and the 4 phase checkpoints are recorded, with a push after each phase. (1) Task 1.4 was added after the Phase 1 checkpoint to fix the review's blocker: heredoc markers are detected only outside quotes, so printf "x << y" cannot swallow a real redirect; the Phase 1 checkpoint predates it. (2) The masker blanks only >/=> characters inside quoted spans (quoted targets still parse), keeps the marker line scanned, and ends a heredoc body at the delimiter line. (3) The README/docs limit is scoped to the redirect scan; tee/sed -i keep the raw command, so prose containing those words can still be denied, and command substitution/helper scripts remain the residual.
